places.name: Haywood Hollywood Horses
places.address: Firestone Ranch, 35100 Anthony Road, Santa Clarita, CA 91390

placement.address: Agua Dulce / Santa Clarita · Haywood Hollywood Horses
placement.reason: The story is in Agua Dulce. Production designer Ruth De Jong confirms practical adjoining ranches, not a different region standing for the town. The point follows the documented original house/corral site at Firestone Ranch. The movie house was built for production and dismantled; the remaining ranch and stables are the real site.

places.name: Jupiter’s Claim
places.address: Agua Dulce Movie Ranch, 34855 Petersen Road, Agua Dulce, CA 91390

placement.reason: The named Agua Dulce park was built at this original ranch. Its main street and Star Lasso arena are one story destination, not separate pins. Production designer Ruth De Jong confirms the working local ranch geography. The entrance was a separate Acton component; the later Universal Studios tour rebuild is not the story location.

audit.subject: Selection
audit.decision: Three strongly supported northern-county places: two central Nope ranch/park settings and the recurring Santa Clarita Diet home. No episode-only TV stops.

audit.subject: Nope
audit.decision: The original rural sets are distinguished from the later Universal tour replica. Source coordinates are original-set points, not mailing-address geocodes. Park and Star Lasso arena count once.

audit.subject: Duel / Chuck’s Cafe
audit.decision: Researched but not added. The opening shows travel north out of Los Angeles via the Palmdale/Lancaster exit and the venue confirms production at Le Chene. The story’s exact cafe/county is not independently established; generic California-highway geography does not prove a Santa Clarita story address.

audit.subject: T2 desert compound / Cactus Jack’s
audit.decision: Lancaster production locations do not prove that Enrique’s fictional compound or the associated roadside stop is in Lancaster. Charon Mesa is not a located canonical LA County address; not added as a northern story pin.

audit.subject: Weeds / Agrestic
audit.decision: The fictional town is placed in the San Fernando Valley. Its Stevenson Ranch exteriors therefore would not establish northern story geography.

audit.subject: Familiar Antelope Valley stand-ins
audit.decision: Kill Bill’s Texas chapel, Palm Springs’ namesake story, Nevada motels, and other out-of-LA story stand-ins were not included merely because filmed locally.

audit.subject: Photographs
audit.decision: All screen images are actual film/TV frames. Two Nope site views are explicitly aerials of original sites, not current standing sets. The Hammond site image is undated Street View, labeled accordingly.
